title: SEE 2082 (2026) Computer Science (Optional Second) - RE-3031'B'
sourceNote: Transcribed and translated in full to English from a scanned SEE 2082 (2026) Computer Science (Optional Second) question paper, code RE-3031'B'. Only the English wording printed on the paper is used here. The paper's own margin notes confirm the section-wise marks split of Group A = 10, Group B = 24, Group C = 16, which matches the printed sub-question breakdown and the full marks of 50 exactly, so no marks discrepancy is flagged. The paper did not state which province issued it, so 'province' is left null - please confirm. 'examBoard' is set to the generic 'SEE' as no specific board name was printed. Question 7's printed main module calls PRINT LongestName$ (Z$) even though Z$ is never assigned a value anywhere in the main module (only A$, B$, C$ are read via DATA/READ and shared via DIM SHARED); the FUNCTION LongestName$ itself never actually uses its Z$ parameter internally either (it works entirely off the shared A$/B$/C$), so this does not affect the two questions actually asked about this program (identifying the global variables and explaining the $ suffix) - preserved exactly as printed, flagged here for awareness. No figures, flowcharts, or diagrams appear anywhere in this paper, so no items include an image field.

blocks.heading: SEE 2082 (2026) Computer Science - Optional Second
blocks.paragraph: This is the Secondary Education Examination (SEE) 2082 (2026 AD) question paper for Computer Science, Optional Second subject, paper code RE-3031'B'. It carries full marks of 50 and an allotted time of 2 hours, divided into Group A (short, one-line answers and terminology), Group B (short/medium answers including QBASIC program tracing and debugging), and Group C (numerical conversions and full program-writing questions in QBASIC and C).

questionSections.title: Group B - Q5: Dry run the given program

items.question: Write the output of the given program. Show it in a dry run table.
items.code:
DECLARE SUB Series (A)
CLS
A = 5
CALL Series (A)
END

SUB Series (A)
 FOR K = 1 TO 5
    PRINT A;
    A = A*2
 NEXT K
END SUB

questionSections.title: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

items.question: Rewrite the given program after correcting the bugs.
items.code:
REM to add record in a existing file
CLS
OPEN "See.dat" for OUTPUT AS #2
BB:
  INPUT "Enter the Name"; N$
  INPUT "Enter the Address"; A$
  INPUT "Enter the Class"; C
  INPUT #2, N$, A$, C
  INPUT "More record"; Y$
  IF UCASE (Y$) = "Y" THEN GOTO BB
CLOSE "See.dat"
END

questionSections.title: Group B - Q7: Study the given program and answer the questions

items.question: Write the Global variables used in the above program.
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
DIM SHARED A$, B$, C$
CLS
READ A$, B$, C$
DATA "NEPAL", "BANGLADESH", "BHUTAN"
PRINT LongestName$ (Z$)
END

FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
  L$=A$
  IF LEN(B$) > LEN(L$) THEN
     L$ = B$
  ELSEIF LEN (C$)>LEN(L$) THEN
     L$=C$
  END IF
  LongestName$=L$
END FUNCTION
items.ocrFlag: The main module calls PRINT LongestName$ (Z$), but Z$ is never assigned a value anywhere in the main module, and the function itself never actually uses its Z$ parameter (it only compares the shared A$, B$, C$). Preserved exactly as printed since it doesn't affect this question.

items.question: Why is the $ (dollar) sign used after the function name?
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
DIM SHARED A$, B$, C$
CLS
READ A$, B$, C$
DATA "NEPAL", "BANGLADESH", "BHUTAN"
PRINT LongestName$ (Z$)
END

FUNCTION LongestName$ (Z$)
  L$=A$
  IF LEN(B$) > LEN(L$) THEN
     L$ = B$
  ELSEIF LEN (C$)>LEN(L$) THEN
     L$=C$
  END IF
  LongestName$=L$
END FUNCTION
